clue.text: Old county partly, or entirely associated with 27

definitions.meaning: historic English counties were divided into administrative districts with this name
a full proportion out of 27 (per cent) is the whole count, so complete means a full figure of this many

explanation.walkthrough: 27 is PER CENT; 'one hundred per cent' means entirely. A hundred was also an old subdivision of an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A county subdivision had this name in old England, and the figure is what a complete percentage reaches.

clue.text: Stormy night began — request sheltering outdoor plants?

indicators.note: one piece covers and protects another, holding it inside
a stormy sea is churned up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: to request is to ask

explanation.surface: A gardener on a stormy night begs someone to protect the plants outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy' rearranges NIGHT BEGAN into HANGINGBET; 'sheltering' puts ASK inside it after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark marks a definition by example: a suspended container is a familiar home for flowers outdoors.

clue.text: In France, she is able to look up for part of Jumbo

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: able means can, as in being able to
elle is the French word for she

explanation.surface: A French woman is able to examine a part of a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to look up' reads the word for able from the bottom, as a down clue allows; 'is' is a link. Jumbo is a jumbo jet, not an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is the streamlined housing for an engine on an aircraft such as a jumbo jet.

clue.text: Fellow's abandoned being playful and taking a chance

indicators.note: the fellow is left behind, so his letter drops out of the word

parts.note: frisky means lively and playful
F is the standard abbreviation for fellow; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A man has given up horsing around and decided to gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' removes F from FRISKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazardous involves taking a chance, so the adjective describes a gamble.

clue.text: Connection via Central Line to Circle Line

definitions.text: Connection via Central Line to Circle Line

parts.words: Connection via Central Line to Circle Line
parts.note: reads like London Underground directions, but describes a straight line through the centre that joins two points on a circle

explanation.surface: Travel directions for changing from one London Tube line to another.
explanation.walkthrough: The Central and Circle lines are London Underground lines; here they are geometry terms.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this chord passes through the centre and links opposite points on the circumference.

clue.text: Painful parting of Romeo and Juliet, perhaps embracing

indicators.note: one word holds another in its arms, wrapped around it

parts.note: Juliet is an example of a young woman, an old word for which is wench
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The heartbreaking separation of Shakespeare's lovers, perhaps while they hug.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo and Juliet look like a pair, but Romeo gives only R and Juliet is a sample young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a sudden distressing separation, such as leaving a loved place or person.

clue.text: Rather unusual exit

definitions.meaning: an informal phrase for something odd or eccentric
the door or route by which one leaves

explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated phrase is slang for bizarre and also the sign marking the door out.

clue.text: I may find treasured relics in digs once occupied

definitions.text: I may find treasured relics in digs once occupied

parts.words: I may find treasured relics in digs once occupied
parts.note: digs suggests lodgings, but means archaeological sites where earlier people once lived

explanation.surface: A lodger finds keepsakes in rooms that someone used to rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' is British slang for rented lodgings; here it means archaeological sites.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who digs up ancient sites is an archaeologist working as a digger of buried remains.

clue.text: Body found in town hall barrister heard about

indicators.note: the word is listened to rather than read, so a word with the same sound is meant

parts.note: a barrister acting in court is referred to as counsel

explanation.surface: A corpse turns up in the town hall, and a lawyer hears about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word; the corpse in the surface is really a governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: A local authority is a governing body that meets in the town hall.

clue.text: Needed the money?

definitions.meaning: British slang calls cash for a purpose the ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'The necessary' is informal British English for the money needed to pay for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential things are required, and slang names the needed cash with the same word.

clue.text: Be steaming, about to take offence

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to take a huff is to take offence

explanation.surface: Someone fuming is about to get offended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' is a link; 'steaming' suggests anger but means the puffing of a steam engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam train chuffs as it puffs along, making the sound of escaping steam.

clue.text: Where documents are found by queue of ministers?

definitions.meaning: office furniture with drawers holding papers
read as a line of filing government ministers, the cabinet in single file

explanation.definitionFit: Office drawers store paperwork, and whimsically a governing body walking in single file.

clue.text: Set on one's Scottish island

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: one is I, and the 's is S
to set something down is to lay it

explanation.surface: Someone is placed on their own Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in an across clue means the second piece follows the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, famous for whisky.

clue.text: Ambiguous representation of a very old clique

indicators.note: the letters are shown in a new form, a rearranged version

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A depiction of an ancient exclusive group is open to interpretation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation of' rearranges A, V, O and CLIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivocal language admits two meanings, so it is deliberately unclear.

clue.text: Agree to differ about rejecting fish, where there's doubt

indicators.note: one piece goes around another
letters that differ are made different, so the word is rearranged
a thing rejected is turned back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Two people decide to disagree about turning a fish away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to differ' shuffles the first word into GREEA; 'rejecting' gives YAR, and 'about' wraps the shuffled letters around it.
explanation.definitionFit: An unclear situation with no definite rule is a zone of doubt or uncertainty.

clue.text: Morals you abandoned, behaving so?

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who has thrown off their morals is behaving lovingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges MORALS and YOU; the whole clue also describes amorous behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping one's scruples suggests acting with romantic desire, which describes the adverb.

clue.text: Priest's garment, by end 'of Communion, is hot

parts.note: a stole is a scarf-like vestment worn by a priest

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A priest's vestment, worn at the end of a church service, is very warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' is slang for stolen goods; STOLE plus N, the end of Communion.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for goods recently taken illegally, so stolen property.

clue.text: Approval of how hikers present requests

definitions.meaning: a gesture of agreement or a go-ahead
hitchhikers ask for a lift by holding out a hand with digit raised

explanation.definitionFit: The raised-digit gesture signals assent and is also what hitchhikers show passing drivers.

clue.text: A problem with hedges, mostly just by a river

indicators.note: most of the word is used, with its last letter removed

parts.note: a maze made of hedges is a puzzle to find the way through
on can mean next to, as in a town on the coast

explanation.surface: A gardener's trouble with overgrown hedges, close to a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the hedge puzzle; the final 'a' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is the great South American river, the largest by volume.

clue.text: Part of exhaust rally-driver needed, coming from Perth?

indicators.note: only a part of these words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A rally driver needs part of the car's exhaust.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth is in Western Australia, so 'coming from Perth' means southern, as in Australian.
explanation.definitionFit: Austral means southern, and Perth lies in the southern land of Australia.

clue.text: Like a child to be smart, overcoming English problem

indicators.note: one piece goes over another, covering it from both sides

parts.note: chic means smart, stylish
a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: Being stylish helps one get past a difficulty with the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcoming' puts E and the difficulty inside the word for smart; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubic describes the plump innocent face of an angelic small child.

clue.text: Trite remark made by newly wed, out of order

indicators.note: one piece sits outside another, wrapped around it

parts.note: a bride is a woman newly married
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A newlywed's cliched comment, said out of turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' looks like a remark on behaviour; OM is the British Order of Merit, an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromide is a dull platitude, originally from the sedative of that name.

clue.text: Traditional type of horse — a hard worker

definitions.meaning: the wooden horse of Troy, from Greek legend
to work like a ... is to work very hard

explanation.definitionFit: The legendary wooden horse is named for Troy, and a tireless worker is likened to its people.

clue.text: Greeting novelty in the pecking order?

definitions.text: Greeting novelty in the pecking order?

parts.words: Greeting novelty in the pecking order?
parts.note: pecking order suggests rank, but here it means an order for pecks, kisses delivered as a novelty greeting

explanation.surface: A new way of saying hello within a social hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: A peck is a quick kiss; the novelty message is ordered and delivered with kisses.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelty message delivered by someone who kisses the recipient, a greeting ordered with pecks.

clue.text: First of officers brought in to search the valley

indicators.note: a letter is brought into a word, placed inside it

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Police officers are called in to search a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' gives O and 'brought in to' puts it inside COMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A coomb is a short valley or hollow, especially on a hillside in southern England.

clue.text: Officer making announcement had one in tears

definitions.meaning: a town officer who calls out public news
read cryptically, one who weeps, a person in tears

explanation.definitionFit: A town official calls out notices, and anyone who weeps is literally one who cries.

clue.text: Ring, rejecting rubbish by American

indicators.note: a thing rejected is turned back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: rot means rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone telephones to refuse an American's garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns ROT into TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A torus is a ring-shaped surface, like a doughnut, in geometry.

clue.text: Very recently delivered one article to an emperor

parts.note: just in means newly arrived
one is I, the Roman numeral
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fresh delivery of an item is brought to the emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Justinian I was the Byzantine emperor famous for codifying Roman law.

clue.text: Take advantage of 'drama being broadcast

parts.note: a play is a drama
a show that is on is being transmitted

explanation.surface: Exploit a play that is on the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit a weakness or feeling is to work on it for advantage.

clue.text: Proportion being observant, but missing palindrome

indicators.note: something missing has been taken away

parts.note: percipient means perceptive, observant
the run IPI reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: Someone is being watchful, yet overlooks a word that reads the same backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The palindrome is not spelt out in the clue: it is a three-letter run inside the word for observant; 'being' and 'but' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A percentage is a proportion expressed out of a hundred.
